title: Choose the visual world for Camellab
question: The roll assigned Poster Session. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Poster Session
options.lineage: AI conference poster sessions (NeurIPS, ICML, ACL)
options.thesis: The lab introduces itself the way researchers do: one big, plainly gridded poster you can read from three metres away.
options.viewport: An ultramarine title band with CAMELLAB in huge condensed caps and the lab line as the affiliation row; below it a strict three-column grid: 1 About the lab, 2 Latest news, 3 Articles, plus a Join box where a poster's QR code would sit.
options.risk: Plain white boxes on a grid go bland if the title band is timid or the grid is loose.

raised.raise: Rank by grid span, not type size: three type sizes in the whole system.
Recency as weight: the newest post always takes the widest panel.
One colour per category held site-wide: news in ultramarine, articles in green.
Provenance on every post: author and date set like a citation line.
Every post card banded with category, date and reading time.

options.label: arXiv Preprint
options.thesis: The site reads like the lab's own paper: title, authors, abstract, numbered sections, footnotes.
options.viewport: A centred paper title, an affiliation line, then a boxed Abstract that is the about-the-lab text, followed by 1. News and 2. Articles as numbered sections.
options.risk: The academic-serif editorial look is also where many runs in this category land; can feel quiet.

options.label: Lab Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase 'camellab' cropped off the edge, and every news item and article is a flat colour tile.
options.viewport: Black ground, a cropped giant wordmark, then a square-tile grid of the latest posts with the about text in a single wide tile.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, since posts map naturally to tiles; it holds on clarity but loses on audience, because this form has no link to research culture.
options.risk: Reads as a phone-OS homage if the type is not giant and the tiles not strict.

options.label: Treasure Map
options.thesis: Navigation as inference across a weathered map.
options.viewport: A whole-page map with posts as landmarks.
options.risk: Hides the lab behind a puzzle.
options.case: Loses on audience and clarity: visitors came to learn about the lab, not to solve a map.
options.kept: Provenance: every post carries author and date like a citation.

options.label: Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page as a live fluid simulation.
options.viewport: A full-screen ink basin with the lab name in the margin.
options.risk: Heavy GPU spectacle and not simple.
options.case: Loses on both axes: striking, but it says nothing about the lab and buries the news.
options.kept: The newest post always carries the most weight.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Sections strung along a perforated rail.
options.viewport: A frame rail crossing an orange field.
options.risk: Film culture is foreign to the audience.
options.case: Loses on both axes for an AI lab's news site.
options.kept: Rank by grid span rather than many type sizes.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.viewport: A dusk garden with bending labels.
options.case: Loses on both axes: no connection to the lab or its writing.
options.kept: One colour per category, held consistently.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.viewport: Posts as labelled jars on shelves.
options.kept: Metadata bands: category, date and reading time on every post.

canonCard.label: The AI lab standard
canonCard.thesis: What AI labs usually ship, done well: dark hero, gradient glow, mission line, team grid, publications.
canonCard.viewport: A dark full-screen hero with a one-line mission and two buttons, then team and publication cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other AI lab by design.
